title: Grid Word Trace

story.briefing: The access code is written across the floor plates, one letter per plate, traced by walking between neighbouring plates without stepping on the same plate twice.
story.success: Code traced across the plates. The final door acknowledges.

description: Given a grid of single characters and a word, return true if the word can be traced by starting at any cell and moving repeatedly to a cell directly above, below, left or right. No cell may be used more than once in a single trace. An empty word is always traceable and returns true.

examples.explanation: The single cell cannot be reused.

hints: Try every cell as a possible starting point, then walk outward matching one letter at a time.
Marking a cell as used before recursing and unmarking it afterwards is the whole of backtracking. Forget the unmark and later traces will find the grid mysteriously blocked.
From a cell matching the current letter, mark it, then try all four neighbours against the next letter. Unmark before returning. Stop immediately when the whole word has matched.
